title: Agent Builder's Playbook — Sep 8, 2026
intro: This edition leans on measured numbers: a 34% real-world-compliance gap hiding behind green tests, a 67% cost cut from smarter model routing, and a git config field that lets an untrusted repo run code before your sandbox ever sees it.

cards.title: Add review-constraint checks to your coding agent's eval, not just pass/fail tests
cards.problem: A coding agent's patch can pass every functional test and still be unmergeable in a real review.
cards.apply: Extract acceptance rules from your own PR review history (style, scope, no-dead-code, no-unrelated-refactor) and run them as a second, separate gate alongside functional tests — don't fold them into the same pass/fail score.
cards.result: SWE-Gate found 221 of 644 functionally-passing repairs (about 34%) violated real review constraints, so a functional-only eval overstates how close an agent is to production-ready.

evidence.note: SWE-Gate's own benchmark run measured the 221/644 non-compliance rate across 75 repositories.

cards.title: Route coding tasks through a cheap-model-first cascade instead of always calling your frontier model
cards.problem: Always sending every coding task to your most capable (and most expensive) model wastes spend on tasks a cheaper model could already solve.
cards.apply: Classify each incoming task's difficulty, let an efficient model draft first, and only escalate to a stronger model — or add an independent-critique-and-revise pass — when a quality gate flags the draft as insufficient.
cards.result: GitHub's HydraFusion cut cost 67% with a 4.9-point quality gain on TerminalBench 2.1 versus always calling the Opus 5 baseline, and 65% cheaper at roughly flat quality on CheckpointBench.

evidence.note: GitHub reports controlled offline evaluation results across three benchmarks (TerminalBench 2.1, DeepSWE, CheckpointBench).

cards.title: Sanitize git config on background context-gathering calls before an untrusted repo can run code
cards.problem: Coding agents run git commands like `git status` in the background to gather context, often before any prompt or sandbox check — and a repo's `.git/config` can name an external program to run during that refresh.
cards.apply: Explicitly disable dangerous config keys on every background git call your agent makes, e.g. run `git -c core.fsmonitor=false status` instead of a bare `git status`, so a malicious `fsmonitor` entry in an untrusted repo's config can't execute.
cards.result: Manifold Security reports this closes the GitSpawn path where opening a repo shipped as a .zip, shared drive, or USB stick — with its `.git` directory intact — runs an attacker's command with the developer's full privileges, outside any sandbox.

evidence.note: Manifold Security's disclosed vulnerability and its own recommended mitigation; not an independently measured before/after result.

cards.title: Move your MCP server off session pinning to survive redeploys without dropping agent connections
cards.problem: Under the old MCP spec, a client opens a session and stays pinned to one server instance, so a redeploy or scale-out kills every live agent session and forces sticky routing plus a shared session store.
cards.apply: Adopt the current MCP spec's stateless mode so clients issue independent requests with no server-side session state to pin to, removing the sticky-routing and session-store requirement entirely.
cards.result: LangChain's MCP integration reports that a redeploy no longer kills live sessions, because there are none left to kill.

evidence.note: LangChain's own description of the stateless spec's operational benefit; no separate before/after measurement given.

cards.title: Mark advanced MCP tool permissions as optional scopes instead of bundling them into one all-or-nothing grant
cards.problem: An agent that needs broad access for its most advanced actions (say, reading inventory, writing prices, and processing refunds) forces every user into an all-or-nothing choice: approve everything, or bounce off the consent screen.
cards.apply: Split your OAuth scope request into required and `optional_scopes`, and have your app inspect which scopes a token actually carries at runtime — disabling the affected feature gracefully instead of failing when an optional one is withheld.
cards.result: Cloudflare reports its optional-scopes support lets users deselect individual permissions at consent, so an agent runs with a narrower default risk profile while still offering the advanced capabilities as opt-in.

evidence.note: Cloudflare's own feature announcement; the benefit is a security-design claim, not a measured incident-rate reduction.

cards.title: Add conflicting-context probes to your tool-using agent's eval suite before you trust it in production
cards.problem: A tool-using agent has to reconcile user instructions, its own parametric knowledge, and live tool/environment observations — and when those disagree, a missed conflict can propagate straight into a tool call.
cards.apply: Build test cases that deliberately contradict the agent across three angles — a stale fact vs. a fresh tool result, an instruction that conflicts with prior context, and a time-dependent fact from two sources — and check whether the agent flags the conflict instead of silently picking one side.
cards.result: KC-Bench tested 9 frontier models (including DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GLM-5.2, and MiniMax-M3) across 238 tasks and found none handled factual correction, identity consistency, and temporal conflict resolution reliably across all settings.

evidence.note: KC-Bench's own benchmark evaluation across 9 models and 238 manually-screened tasks.

cards.title: Batch background task results and stop over-compressing tool output to cut agent cost
cards.problem: Teams chase cost savings by shortening every tool response, but a concise response that omits information the agent needs just forces extra recovery calls — costing more, not less.
cards.apply: Deliver finished background task results directly instead of making the agent issue a separate retrieval call for each one, and reserve output compression for predictable noise like build/install/test logs — never for source code or search results.
cards.result: GitHub measured a 2.3% cost cut from batching background-task completions (collapsing four calls into two) and a 5.5% cut from selective log compression, with no quality regression across Copilot CLI and code review.

evidence.note: GitHub reports measured cost deltas per technique from its own benchmarks and online experiments.
